A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Cond-FiP and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Matching relocated and renumbered content supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments on synthetic SCMs, CSuite, and Sachs data, including ablations, distribution-shift tests, and counterfactual-generation results.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds Ecoli evaluation, graph-perturbation experiments, and a pretraining-scale study.

M1.justification: The dataset encoder, conditional codebooks, adaptive normalization, training objectives, and fixed-point generation procedure are retained. Algorithms 1–2 document the existing method. Joint and curriculum training are suggested as future work, not implemented changes.

E1.justification: v4 adds observational-generation evaluation on the 46-variable Ecoli dataset (Table 2) and controlled missing-edge inputs (Appendix F.1). AVICI, CSuite including Gaussian-mixture noise, Sachs, and the existing task families remain covered.

E2.justification: DoWhy, DECI, FiP, and CausalNF retain their participation in corresponding comparisons, including DoWhy's exclusion at 50 samples. Ecoli uses the existing main baseline set, and the new graph-perturbation analysis uses FiP; no existing comparison loses or gains a method.

E3.justification: New protocols test edge-removal proportions of 0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, and 0.1 for 100-node RFF OUT sample generation, and pretraining on 100,000, 400,000, and 1 million SCMs against the retained 4-million setting for 20-node graphs. Ecoli uses 400 context and 400 query samples. Existing evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices F.1 and G.1 add two targeted sample-generation analyses: sensitivity to missing graph edges and dependence on pretraining scale. Existing encoder/decoder ablations, distribution-shift tests, scarce-data experiments, larger-context tests, and counterfactual analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 7's caption now explicitly identifies means and standard errors across 12 scenarios; v3 described RMSE across those scenarios without identifying the uncertainty statistic. The plotted uncertainty and existing mean/standard-error table practice are retained. No repeated-run counts, seeds, or significance-testing procedure are added.

E6.justification: New entries cover Ecoli, graph corruption, and smaller pretraining budgets. Ecoli generation MMD is 0.019 for Cond-FiP, 0.017 for FiP, 0.016 for DECI, and 0.020 for DoWhy. Section 4.2 also adds a 36-versus-180-hour runtime estimate across 360 tasks. All 30 existing table bodies and the retained figure graphics are unchanged.

T1.justification: The SCM assumptions, DAG-attention formulation, fixed-point generation argument, and invertibility derivation in Appendix A.1–A.3 are retained. The added pseudocode does not introduce a new theoretical result or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction explicitly qualify the target as causal-mechanism inference conditioned on observational data and a causal graph, clarifying v3's broader abstract wording about SCM inference. The central novelty, parameter-free adaptation, competitive performance, and scarce-data claims remain.

C2.justification: v4 interprets graph-perturbation results as evidence of graph-conditioned mechanism learning and the scale study as showing diminishing returns from additional pretraining. It also discusses joint or curriculum encoder training as possible extensions. Existing limitations concerning synthetic training, larger contexts, counterfactuals, and Sachs interventions remain.

D1.justification: v4 adds encoder/decoder pseudocode, an explicit CSuite task list, and training/inference timings. It removes the anonymous-code appendix and folder guidance while retaining the public repository footnote. Main hyperparameters and hardware are unchanged. Algorithm 1 introduces an unreconciled negative-infinity mask convention, whereas Section 3.1 subtracts a positive-infinity mask.

R1.justification: Related work adds recent causal-effect/PFN studies, gene-regulatory discovery, and broader meta-learning/ICL references. Section 2.1 explicitly distinguishes prior-fitted networks from emergent LLM in-context learning. Scutari's bnlearn reference is added and Gretton's MMD reference removed. The central positioning around amortized causal-mechanism learning remains.

P1.justification: Related Works moves from Section 5 to Section 1.1, while CSuite-GMM and Sachs discussion moves into the main experiments. The abstract, amortized-inference explanation, and selected experimental passages are expanded or edited. Most method and existing appendix prose is closely retained.

P2.justification: The document is globally retypeset in TMLR format, changing typography, text width, running headers, and float placement throughout. Three tables and two algorithm displays are added. The existing Figure 7 and Sachs table move into the main text, with revised captions; all seven underlying figure graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: Ecoli evaluation and the graph-error and pretraining-scale analyses add useful evidence missing from v3, while clearer scope and quantitative runtime information improve assessability. These gains are incremental: the original results and major limitations remain unchanged. Added pseudocode helps documentation, although its mask-sign inconsistency with Section 3.1 limits that benefit.
